text:
maria: quick q — we have a few shell scripts in infra that call `rwd-cli` and assume tokens are on disk. for CI we want ephemeral tokens (short lived) and avoid writing creds to runners. what's the established pattern?

samir: we usually rely on `RWD_API_KEY` in CI, set as secret, and avoid disk. for local/dev machines we use `rwd login --profile work` which writes into keyring.

maria: right but one of the scripts does `rwd auth get --profile work --format=json > ~/.rwd/creds.json` for legacy tooling. I'd prefer a minimal change to support ephemeral tokens in workflows.

tj: option A: keep env var for CI and update scripts to `if [ -n \"$RWD_API_KEY\" ]; then echo \\\"$RWD_API_KEY\\\"; else rwd auth get --profile work --raw; fi` — simplest.

irene: +1. also add `--no-keyring` flag note for windows CI images where keyring fails. we had a flakiness with Windows runner hitting credential manager popups.

maria: good point — is there a `rwd auth` subcommand that prints token raw? I remember a `--raw` but fuzzy.

devex-bot: helper: `rwd auth current --format token` prints just the token (non-interactive).`

samir: new suggestion — create a small wrapper `rwd-cred` in repo root that centralizes logic: export token or fall back to `rwd auth current`. Then all scripts call `./scripts/rwd-cred`. Allows single change for CI vs local.

maria: sketch of wrapper I pushed as gist:
```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
# scripts/rwd-cred
if [ -n "$RWD_API_KEY" ]; then
  echo "$RWD_API_KEY"
elif [ -n "$RWD_PROFILE" ]; then
  rwd auth current --profile "$RWD_PROFILE" --format token
else
  rwd auth current --format token
fi
```

tj: looks good. can we add a TTL check so CI fails fast if token expired? maybe `rwd auth inspect` exists?

samir: `rwd auth inspect --format json` returns exp timestamp. simple jq check: `rwd auth inspect | jq -r .expires_at` then compare epoch. add exit code 2 if expired.

maria: added that to the gist and created a tiny PR: #4823. @tj can you quick review? it's tiny. also left note to avoid printing tokens in logs (use `set +x`).

tj: will review today. one more note: streaming clients (go/python SDK) keep a long-lived connection; if token rotates mid-stream we had reconnect glitches. not relevant for quick scripts but be aware if your script spawns a persistent process.

irene: true — for long runners we recommend a service account token with longer TTL on dedicated hosts, or use our token refresh library inside the service.

maria: cool. last question — windows devs: any preference for storing profiles? keyring vs file?

samir: keyring by default. but devs on Windows WSL prefer plain file at `~/.rwd/profile` shared via symlink. we added a `rwd config set storage file` option in earlier PRs — check `rwd config --help`.

maria: perfect. thanks all — I'll merge #4823 once tj signs off and update the infra scripts to call `./scripts/rwd-cred`. :thumbsup:

tj: left a tiny nit about error message text, otherwise LGTM.

maria: addressed the nit, force-pushed. merging now.

samir: nice! once merged we should add a line to the CLI FAQ about `--no-keyring` and `RWD_API_KEY` for CI.

maria: added a TODO in the docs backlog. thanks everyone.
